text: Preface
translated: 前言

text:
In the decade since the first edition, this book has become a staple of undergraduate
and graduate courses at universities around the world. It has also found a home on
the bookshelves of practitioners at companies large and small. The audience for the
book has, in turn, advanced the state of the art in multiprocessor programming. In
this second edition, we aim to continue this “virtuous cycle” by providing new and
updated content. Our goal is the same as with the first edition: to provide a textbook
for a senior-level undergraduate course and a reference for practitioners.
translated: 自第一版出版以来的十年里，本书已成为世界各地大学本科生和研究生课程的核心教材。它也已进入大大小小公司从业者的书架。反过来，本书的读者也推动了多处理器编程领域的前沿发展。在第二版中，我们旨在通过提供新的和更新的内容来延续这种“良性循环”。我们的目标与第一版相同：为高年级本科生课程提供教材，为从业者提供参考书。

text: Organization
translated: 组织

text:
The first part of this book covers the principles of concurrent programming, show-
ing how to think as a concurrent programmer, developing fundamental skills such
as understanding when operations “happen,” considering all possible interleavings,
and identifying impediments to progress. Like many skills—driving a car, cooking
a meal, or appreciating caviar—thinking concurrently must be cultivated, and it can
be learned with moderate effort. Readers who want to start programming right away
may skip most of this section but should still read Chapters 2 and 3, which cover the
basic ideas necessary to understand the rest of the book.
translated: 本书的第一部分涵盖了并发编程的原则，展示了如何像并发程序员一样思考，培养基本技能，例如理解操作何时“发生”、考虑所有可能的交织执行，以及识别阻碍进展的因素。像许多技能一样——开车、做菜或欣赏鱼子酱——并发思维必须通过培养获得，并且可以通过适度的努力来学会。想要立即开始编程的读者可以跳过本节的大部分内容，但仍应阅读第2章和第3章，它们涵盖了理解本书其余部分所需的基本概念。

text:
We first look at the classic mutual exclusion problem (Chapter 2). This chapter
is essential for understanding why concurrent programming is a challenge. It covers
basic concepts such as fairness and deadlock. We then ask what it means for a con-
current program to be correct (Chapter 3). We consider several alternative conditions
and the circumstances under which one might want to use each one. We examine
the properties of shared memory essential to concurrent computation (Chapter 4),
and we look at the kinds of synchronization primitives needed to implement highly
concurrent data structures (Chapters 5 and 6).
translated: 我们首先介绍经典的互斥问题（第2章）。本章对于理解并发编程为何具有挑战性至关重要。它涵盖了公平性和死锁等基本概念。然后我们探讨并发程序正确性的含义（第3章）。我们考察几种替代条件以及在何种情况下可能想要使用每一种条件。我们研究共享内存的特性，这些特性对于并发计算至关重要（第4章），并探讨实现高并发数据结构所需的同步原语类型（第5章和第6章）。

text:
We think it is essential that anyone who wants to become truly skilled in the art
of multiprocessor programming spend time solving the problems presented in the
first part of this book. Although these problems are idealized, they distill the kind
of thinking necessary to write effective multiprocessor programs. Most importantly,
they distill the style of thinking necessary to avoid the common mistakes committed
by nearly all novice programmers when they first encounter concurrency.
translated: 我们认为，任何想要真正掌握多处理器编程艺术的人，都必须花时间解决本书第一部分提出的问题。虽然这些问题是理想化的，但它们提炼了编写高效多处理器程序所需的思维方式。最重要的是，它们提炼了避免几乎所有新手程序员在首次接触并发时都会犯的常见错误所需的思维风格。

text:
The second part of the book describes the practice of concurrent programming.
For most of this part, we give examples in Java to avoid getting mired in low-level
details. However, we have expanded this edition to include discussion of some low-
level issues that are essential to understanding multiprocessor systems and how to
program them effectively. We use examples in C++ to illustrate these issues.
translated: 本书的第二部分描述了并发编程的实践。在该部分的大多数内容中，我们使用 Java 给出示例，以避免陷入低级细节。然而，我们在本版中扩展了一些对于理解多处理器系统以及如何有效地对其进行编程至关重要的低级问题的讨论。我们用 C++ 示例来说明这些问题。

text:
Each chapter has a secondary theme, illustrating either a particular programming
pattern or an algorithmic technique. Chapter 7 covers spin locks and contention,
and introduces the importance of the underlying architecture: spin lock performance
cannot be understood without understanding the multiprocessor memory hierarchy.
Chapter 8 covers monitor locks and waiting, a common synchronization idiom.
translated: 每章都有次要主题，阐述特定的编程模式或算法技术。第7章涵盖自旋锁和争用，并介绍底层架构的重要性：不了解多处理器内存层次结构，就无法理解自旋锁性能。第8章涵盖监视器锁和等待，这是一种常见的同步习语。

text:
Several chapters cover concurrent data structures. Linked lists, which illustrate
different kinds of synchronization patterns, from coarse-grained locking to fine-
grained locking to lock-free structures, are covered in Chapter 9. This chapter should
be read before the remaining chapters, which depend on it. First-in-first-out (FIFO)
queues illustrate the “ABA problem” that arises when using atomic synchronization
primitives (Chapter 10); stacks illustrate an important synchronization pattern called
elimination (Chapter 11); hash maps show how an algorithm can exploit natural paral-
lelism (Chapter 13); skip lists illustrate efficient parallel search (Chapter 14); priority
queues illustrate how one can sometimes relax correctness guarantees to enhance
performance (Chapter 15).
translated: 多章涵盖并发数据结构。链表（第9章）展示不同种类的同步模式，从粗粒度锁到细粒度锁再到无锁结构。本章应在其他章节之前阅读，因为后续章节依赖于它。先进先出（FIFO）队列演示使用原子同步原语时出现的“ABA问题”（第10章）；栈展示一种称为消除的重要同步模式（第11章）；哈希映射展示算法如何利用自然并行性（第13章）；跳表展示高效并行搜索（第14章）；优先队列展示如何有时通过放宽正确性保证来提升性能（第15章）。

队列演示使用原子同步原语时出现的“ABA问题”（第10章）；栈展示一种称为消除的重要同
步模式（第11章）；哈希映射展示算法如何利用自然并行性（第13章）；跳表展示高效并
行搜索（第14章）；优先队列展示如何有时通过放宽正确性保证来提升性能（第15章）。

text:
We also consider other fundamental problems in concurrent computing. Chap-
ter 12 describes counting and sorting, two classic problems with nuanced concurrent
solutions. Breaking a program into parallelizable tasks and organizing their execu-
tion is an essential skill for concurrent programming, and we consider several ways
to do this, including work stealing and distribution (Chapter 16), data parallelism
(Chapter 17), barriers (Chapter 18), and transactional programming (Chapter 20).
Memory management is another fundamental challenge for concurrent programs, and
we discuss how to manually reclaim memory in Chapter 19. Because Java provides
automatic memory management, we use C++ to illustrate these issues.
translated: 我们还考虑并发计算中的其他基本问题。第12章描述了计数和排序，这是两个具有细微并发解决方案的经典问题。将程序分解为可并行化的任务并组织它们的执行是并发编程的基本技能，我们探讨了几种实现方法，包括工作窃取和分发（第16章）、数据并行（第17章）、屏障（第18章）和事务编程（第20章）。内存管理是并发程序面临的另一个基本挑战，我们在第19章讨论如何手动回收内存。由于Java提供自动内存管理，我们使用C++来说明这些问题。

Much of these latter chapters are new to this edition: Chapters 17 and 19 are com-
pletely new, and Chapters 16 and 20 have been substantially updated from the first
edition. In particular, Chapter 20 now covers hardware primitives for transactional
programming as well as software strategies, and the examples have been recast in
C++ to allow us to focus on lower-level mechanisms.
translated: 这些后续章节中的大部分在本版中是新增的：第17章和第19章是全新的，第16章和第20章较第一版有大幅更新。特别是第20章现在涵盖了事务编程的硬件原语以及软件策略，示例已用C++重写，以便我们专注于底层机制。

text: Prerequisites
translated: 先决条件

text:
The prerequisites for the second edition are largely the same as for the first. To un-
derstand the algorithms and their properties, readers will need some knowledge of
discrete mathematics, especially “big-O” notation and what it means for a problem
to be NP-complete, and data structures such as stacks, queues, lists, balanced trees,
and hash tables. It is also helpful to be familiar with elementary computer architec-
ture and system constructs such as processors, threads, and caches. While a course
on operating systems or computer organization would suffice, neither is necessary;
dozens of universities have used this book successfully without either prerequisite.
translated: 第二版的先修要求与第一版基本相同。为了理解算法及其性质，读者需要具备一些离散数学知识，特别是“大O”符号及其含义，以及NP完全问题的概念，还有栈、队列、列表、平衡树和哈希表等数据结构。熟悉基本的计算机体系结构和系统构造（如处理器、线程和缓存）也会有所帮助。虽然修过操作系统或计算机组织课程就足够了，但这两者都不是必须的；数十所大学在没有这两门先修课的情况下也成功使用了本书。

text: Introduction
translated: 简介

text:
At the dawn of the twenty-first century, the computer industry underwent yet an-
other revolution. The major chip manufacturers had increasingly been unable to make
processor chips both smaller and faster. As Moore’s law approached the end of its
50-year reign, manufacturers turned to “multicore” architectures, in which multiple
processors (cores) on a single chip communicate directly through shared hardware
caches. Multicore chips make computing more effective by exploiting parallelism:
harnessing multiple circuits to work on a single task.
translated: 二十一世纪初，计算机行业经历了另一场革命。主要芯片制造商越来越无法使处理器芯片既更小又更快。随着摩尔定律接近其50年统治的终结，制造商转向了“多核”架构，在这种架构中，单个芯片上的多个处理器（核心）通过共享硬件缓存直接通信。多核芯片通过利用并行性使计算更加高效：利用多个电路协同处理单一任务。

text:
The spread of multiprocessor architectures has had a pervasive effect on how we
develop software. During the twentieth century, advances in technology brought reg-
ular increases in clock speed, so software would effectively “speed up” by itself over
time. In this century, however, that “free ride” has come to an end. Today, advances in
technology bring regular increases in parallelism, but only minor increases in clock
speed. Exploiting that parallelism is one of the outstanding challenges of modern
computer science.
translated: 多处理器架构的普及对我们开发软件的方式产生了深远影响。在二十世纪，技术进步带来了时钟频率的规律性提升，因此软件实际上会随着时间的推移自动“加速”。然而在本世纪，这种“免费午餐”已成为过去。如今，技术进步带来的是并行度的规律性提升，而时钟频率仅有微小增长。利用这种并行性是现代计算机科学面临的杰出挑战之一。

text:
This book focuses on how to program multiprocessors that communicate via
a shared memory. Such systems are often called shared-memory multiprocessors
or, more recently, multicores. Programming challenges arise at all scales of multi-
processor systems—at a very small scale, processors within a single chip need to
coordinate access to a shared memory location, and on a large scale, processors in a
supercomputer need to coordinate the routing of data. Multiprocessor programming
is challenging because modern computer systems are inherently asynchronous: ac-
tivities can be halted or delayed without warning by interrupts, preemption, cache
misses, failures, and other events. These delays are inherently unpredictable, and can
vary enormously in scale: a cache miss might delay a processor for fewer than ten
instructions, a page fault for a few million instructions, and operating system pre-
emption for hundreds of millions of instructions.
translated: 本书专注于如何编程通过共享内存通信的多处理器。此类系统通常称为共享内存多处理器，或最近称为多核处理器。多处理器系统的各个规模都存在编程挑战——在极小规模上，单个芯片内的处理器需要协调对共享内存位置的访问，在大规模上，超级计算机中的处理器需要协调数据路由。多处理器编程具有挑战性，因为现代计算机系统本质上是异步的：活动可能因中断、抢占、缓存未命中、故障和其他事件而毫无预警地停止或延迟。这些延迟本质上是不可预测的，且规模差异巨大：缓存未命中可能延迟处理器不到十条指令，页面错误延迟几百万条指令，操作系统抢占延迟数亿条指令。

text:
We approach multiprocessor programming from two complementary directions:
principles and practice. In the principles part of this book, we focus on computability:
figuring out what can be computed in an asynchronous concurrent environment. We
use an idealized model of computation in which multiple concurrent threads manip-
ulate a set of shared objects. The sequence of the thread operations on the objects is
called the concurrent program or concurrent algorithm. This model is essentially the
model presented by threads in Java, C#, and C++.
translated: 我们从两个互补的方向来探讨多处理器编程：原理和实践。在本书的原理部分，我们关注可计算性：弄清在异步并发环境中可以计算什么。我们使用一个理想化的计算模型，其中多个并发线程操作一组共享对象。线程对对象的操作序列称为并发程序或并发算法。这个模型本质上就是Java、C#和C++中线程所呈现的模型。

共享对象。线程对对象的操作序列称为并发程序或并发算法。这个模型本质上就是Java、C#和C++中
线程所呈现的模型。

text:
Surprisingly, there are easy-to-specify shared objects that cannot be implemented
by any concurrent algorithm. It is therefore important to understand what not to try,
before proceeding to write multiprocessor programs. Many of the issues that will land
multiprocessor programmers in trouble are consequences of fundamental limitations
of the computational model, so we view the acquisition of a basic understanding of
concurrent shared-memory computability as a necessary step. The chapters dealing
with principles take the reader through a quick tour of asynchronous computabil-
ity, attempting to expose various computability issues, and how they are addressed
through the use of hardware and software mechanisms.
translated: 令人惊讶的是，存在易于指定但无法通过任何并发算法实现的共享对象。因此，在着手编写多处理器程序之前，了解不该尝试什么至关重要。许多会让多处理师程序员陷入困境的问题，都是计算模型根本局限性的后果，因此我们认为获得并发共享内存可计算性的基本理解是必要的一步。涉及原理的章节将带领读者快速浏览异步可计算性，试图揭示各种可计算性问题，以及如何通过硬件和软件机制来解决这些问题。

text:
An important step in the understanding of computability is the specification and
verification of what a given program actually does. This is perhaps best described
as program correctness. The correctness of multiprocessor programs, by their very
nature, is more complex than that of their sequential counterparts, and requires a
different set of tools, even for the purpose of “informal reasoning” (which, of course,
is what most programmers actually do).
translated: 理解计算性的重要一步是明确并验证给定程序实际执行的功能。这或许最好描述为程序正确性。多处理器程序的正确性因其本质特性，比其顺序执行的对应程序更为复杂，并需要一套不同的工具，即便仅用于“非形式化推理”（当然，这正是大多数程序员实际所做的）。

text:
Sequential correctness is mostly concerned with safety properties. A safety prop-
erty states that some “bad thing” never happens. For example, a traffic light never
displays green in all directions, even if the power fails. Naturally, concurrent correct-
ness is also concerned with safety, but the problem is much, much harder, because
safety must be ensured despite the vast number of ways that the steps of concurrent
threads can be interleaved. Equally important, concurrent correctness encompasses
a variety of liveness properties that have no counterparts in the sequential world. A
liveness property states that a particular good thing will happen. For example, a red
traffic light will eventually turn green.
translated: 顺序正确性主要关注安全性属性。安全性属性声明某些"坏事"永远不会发生。例如，即使断电，交通灯也不会在所有方向都显示绿灯。自然地，并发正确性也关注安全性，但问题难得多，因为必须确保安全性，尽管并发线程的步骤可以交织的方式数量极大。同样重要的是，并发正确性包含各种活性属性，这些属性在顺序世界中没有对应物。活性属性声明某个特定的好事将会发生。例如，红灯最终会变绿。

A final goal of the part of the book dealing with principles is to introduce a variety
of metrics and approaches for reasoning about concurrent programs, which will later
serve us when discussing the correctness of real-world objects and programs.

text:
The second part of the book deals with the practice of multiprocessor program-
ming, and focuses on performance. Analyzing the performance of multiprocessor
algorithms is also different in flavor from analyzing the performance of sequential
programs. Sequential programming is based on a collection of well-established and
well-understood abstractions. When we write a sequential program, we can often ig-
nore that underneath it all, pages are being swapped from disk to memory, and smaller
units of memory are being moved in and out of a hierarchy of processor caches. This
complex memory hierarchy is essentially invisible, hiding behind a simple program-
ming abstraction.
translated: 本书的第二部分探讨多处理器编程的实践，重点关注性能。分析多处理器算法的性能与分析顺序程序的性能在本质上有所不同。顺序编程建立在一套成熟且透彻理解的抽象之上。编写顺序程序时，我们往往可以忽略底层机制：页面在磁盘与内存间交换，更小的内存单元在处理器缓存层级间移动。这种复杂的内存层级本质上是不可见的，隐藏在简单的编程抽象之后。

text:
In the multiprocessor context, this abstraction breaks down, at least from a perfor-
mance perspective. To achieve adequate performance, programmers must sometimes
“outwit” the underlying memory system, writing programs that would seem bizarre
to someone unfamiliar with multiprocessor architectures. Someday, perhaps, concur-
rent architectures will provide the same degree of efficient abstraction as sequential
architectures, but in the meantime, programmers should beware.
translated: 在多处理器环境中，这种抽象会失效，至少从性能角度来看是这样。为了获得足够的性能，程序员有时必须“智取”底层内存系统，编写出对于不熟悉多处理器架构的人来说显得古怪的程序。也许有一天，并发架构将提供与顺序架构同等程度的高效抽象，但在那之前，程序员应当小心。

The practice part of the book presents a progressive collection of shared objects
and programming tools. Every object and tool is interesting in its own right, and we
use each one to expose the reader to higher-level issues: spin locks illustrate con-
tention, linked lists illustrate the role of locking in data structure design, and so on.
translated: 本书的实践部分展示了一组循序渐进的共享对象和编程工具。每个对象和工具本身都很有趣，我们利用它们向读者揭示更高层面的问题：自旋锁说明了竞争问题，链表说明了锁在数据结构设计中的作用，等等。

Each of these issues has important consequences for program performance. We hope
that readers will understand the issue in a way that will later allow them to apply the
lessons learned to specific multiprocessor systems. We culminate with a discussion
of state-of-the-art technologies such as transactional memory.

For most of this book, we present code in the Java programming language, which
provides automatic memory management. However, memory management is an im-
portant aspect of programming, especially concurrent programming. So, in the last
two chapters, we switch to C++. In some cases, the code presented is simplified
by omitting nonessential details. Complete code for all the examples is available
on the book’s companion website at https://textbooks.elsevier.com/web/product_
details.aspx?isbn=978124159501.

text:
Throughout the book, we avoid presenting specific performance numbers for pro-
grams and algorithms, instead focusing on general trends. There is a good reason
why: multiprocessors vary greatly, and what works well on one machine may work
significantly less well on another. We focus on general trends to ensure that observa-
tions are not tied to specific platforms at specific times.
translated: 本书始终避免呈现程序和算法的具体性能数据，而是关注总体趋势。这样做是有充分理由的：多处理器差异很大，在一台机器上效果很好的方法，在另一台机器上可能效果差得多。我们关注总体趋势，以确保观察结果不受特定平台在特定时间的限制。

text:
On the first day of your new job, your boss asks you to find all primes between 1 and
10<sup>10</sup> (never mind why) using a parallel machine that supports ten concurrent threads.
This machine is rented by the minute, so the longer your program takes, the more it
costs. You want to make a good impression. What do you do?
translated: 入职第一天，老板让你用一台支持十个并发线程的并行机器，找出 1 到 10<sup>10</sup> 之间的所有素数（别问为什么）。这台机器按分钟租用，程序运行越久，费用越高。你想给老板留个好印象。你会怎么办？

text:
approach fails to distribute the work evenly for an elementary but important reason:
Equal ranges of inputs do not produce equal amounts of work. Primes do not occur
uniformly; there are more primes between 1 and 10<sup>9</sup> than between 9 10<sup>9</sup> and1 0 ^ { 1 0 }
To make matters worse, the computation time per prime is not the same in all ranges:
it usually takes longer to test whether a large number is prime than a small number.
In short, there is no reason to believe that the work will be divided equally among the
threads, and it is not clear even which threads will have the most work.
translated: 这种方法由于一个基本但重要的原因，无法均匀分配工作：相等的输入范围不会产生相等的工作量。素数分布不均匀；1 和 10<sup>9</sup> 之间的素数比 9 10<sup>9</sup> 和 1 0 ^ { 1 0 } 之间的更多。更糟糕的是，每个素数的计算时间在不同范围内不相同：测试大数是否为素数通常比测试小数耗时更长。简而言之，没有理由相信工作会在线程间均等分配，甚至不清楚哪些线程会承担最多工作。

text:
A more promising way to split the work among the threads is to assign each thread
one integer at a time (Fig. 1.2). When a thread is finished testing an integer, it asks
for another. To this end, we introduce a shared counter, an object that encapsulates
an integer value, and that provides a getAndIncrement() method, which increments
the counter’s value and returns the counter’s prior value.

text:
Now imagine that two threads call the counter’s getAndIncrement() method at
about the same time, so that they both read 1 from value. In this case, each thread
would set its local temp variables to 1, set value to 2, and return 1. This behavior is
not what we intended: we expect concurrent calls to the counter’s getAndIncrement()
to return distinct values. It could be worse: after one thread reads 1 from value, but
before it sets value to 2, another thread could go through the increment loop several
times, reading 1 and writing 2, then reading 2 and writing 3. When the first thread fi-
nally completes its operation and sets value to 2, it will actually be setting the counter
back from 3 to 2.
translated: 现在假设两个线程几乎在同一时间调用计数器的 getAndIncrement() 方法，导致它们都从 value 读取到 1。在这种情况下，每个线程都会将其局部 temp 变量设为 1，将 value 设为 2，并返回 1。这种行为不是我们预期的：我们期望对计数器 getAndIncrement() 的并发调用返回不同的值。情况可能更糟：在一个线程从 value 读取 1 之后，但在它将 value 设为 2 之前，另一个线程可能多次执行递增循环，读取 1 写入 2，然后读取 2 写入 3。当第一个线程最终完成操作并将 value 设为 2 时，实际上是将计数器从 3 重置回了 2。

The heart of the problem is that incrementing the counter’s value requires two
distinct operations on the shared variable: reading the value field into a temporary
variable and writing it back to the Counter object.

text:
Something similar happens when you try to pass someone approaching you head-
on in a corridor. You may find yourself veering right and then left several times to
avoid the other person doing exactly the same thing. Sometimes you manage to avoid
bumping into them and sometimes you do not. In fact, as we will see in the later
chapters, such collisions are provably unavoidable.<sup>1</sup> On an intuitive level, what is go-
ing on is that each of you is performing two distinct steps: looking at (“reading”) the
other’s current position, and moving (“writing”) to one side or the other. The prob-
lem is, when you read the other’s position, you have no way of knowing whether they
have decided to stay or move. In the same way that you and the annoying stranger
must decide on which side to pass each other, threads accessing a shared Counter
must decide who goes first and who goes second.
translated: 当你试图在走廊里避让迎面走来的人时，会发生类似的情况。你可能会发现自己先向右避让，然后又向左避让，好几次，而对方也在做完全相同的动作。有时你能避免碰撞，有时则不能。事实上，正如我们在后面章节将看到的，这种碰撞在理论上是不可避免的。<sup>1</sup> 直观上讲，你们各自在执行两个不同的步骤：观察（“读取”）对方的当前位置，以及移动（“写入”）到一侧或另一侧。问题在于，当你读取对方位置时，无法知道他们是决定原地不动还是移动。就像你和那个讨厌的陌生人必须决定从哪边通过一样，访问共享 Counter 的线程必须决定谁先走、谁后走。

text:
As we discuss in Chapter 5, modern multiprocessor hardware provides special
read–modify–write instructions that allow threads to read, modify, and write a value
to memory in one atomic (that is, indivisible) hardware step. For the Counter object,
we can use such hardware to increment the counter atomically.
translated: 正如我们在第5章中讨论的，现代多处理器硬件提供了特殊的读-修改-写指令，允许线程在一个原子（即不可分割）硬件步骤中读取、修改并将值写入内存。对于Counter对象，我们可以利用这种硬件来原子性地增加计数器。

text:
We can also ensure atomic behavior by guaranteeing in software (using only read
and write instructions) that only one thread executes the read-and-write sequence at a
time. The problem of ensuring that only one thread can execute a particular block of
code at a time, called the mutual exclusion problem, is one of the classic coordination
problems in multiprocessor programming.
translated: 我们还可以通过在软件中保证（仅使用读和写指令）同一时间只有一个线程执行读写序列，来确保原子行为。确保同一时间只有一个线程能执行特定代码块的问题，称为互斥问题，是多处理器编程中的经典协调问题之一。

text:
As a practical matter, you are unlikely ever to find yourself having to design your
own mutual exclusion algorithm (you would probably call on a library). Nevertheless,
understanding how to implement mutual exclusion from the basics is an essential
condition for understanding concurrent computation in general. There is no more
effective way to learn how to reason about essential and ubiquitous issues such as
mutual exclusion, deadlock, bounded fairness, and blocking versus nonblocking syn-
chronization.
translated: 从实际角度来看，你极不可能需要设计自己的互斥算法（通常会调用库）。然而，理解如何从基础实现互斥是理解并发计算的必要条件。没有比这更有效的方法来学习如何推理互斥、死锁、有界公平性以及阻塞与非阻塞同步等基本且普遍存在的问题。

text: 1.2 A fable
translated: 1.2 一个寓言

text:
Instead of treating coordination problems (such as mutual exclusion) as programming
exercises, we prefer to frame concurrent coordination problems as interpersonal prob-
lems. In the next few sections, we present a sequence of fables, illustrating some of
the basic problems. Like most authors of fables, we retell stories mostly invented by
others (see the chapter notes at the end of this chapter).
translated: 与其将协调问题（如互斥）视为编程练习，我们更倾向于将并发协调问题视为人际问题。在接下来的几节中，我们将通过一系列寓言故事来阐述一些基本问题。像大多数寓言作者一样，我们转述的故事大多由他人创作（详见本章末尾的章节注释）。

text:
Alice and Bob are neighbors, and they share a yard. Alice owns a cat and Bob
owns a dog. Both pets like to run around in the yard, but (naturally) they do not
get along. After some unfortunate experiences, Alice and Bob agree that they should
coordinate to make sure that both pets are never in the yard at the same time. Of
course, they rule out trivial solutions that do not allow either pet into an empty yard,
or that reserve the yard exclusively to one pet or the other.
translated: 爱丽丝和鲍勃是邻居，他们共用一个院子。爱丽丝养了一只猫，鲍勃养了一只狗。两只宠物都喜欢在院子里跑来跑去，但（自然地）它们相处不好。经过一些不幸的经历后，爱丽丝和鲍勃同意应该协调一下，确保两只宠物永远不会同时在院子里。当然，他们排除了那些不允许任何宠物进入空院子、或者把院子专门留给其中一只宠物的琐碎解决方案。

How should they do it? Alice and Bob need to agree on mutually compatible pro-
cedures for deciding what to do. We call such an agreement a coordination protocol
(or just a protocol, for short).

text:
The yard is large, so Alice cannot simply look out of the window to check whether
Bob’s dog is present. She could perhaps walk over to Bob’s house and knock on the
door, but that takes a long time, and what if it rains? Alice might lean out the window
and shout “Hey Bob! Can I let the cat out?” The problem is that Bob might not hear
her. He could be watching TV, visiting his girlfriend, or out shopping for dog food.
They could try to coordinate by cell phone, but the same difficulties arise if Bob is in
the shower, driving through a tunnel, or recharging his phone’s batteries.
translated: 院子很大，所以爱丽丝不能只是透过窗户看看就能确认鲍勃的狗是否在场。她或许可以走到鲍勃家敲门，但那需要很长时间，万一下雨怎么办？爱丽丝可能会探出窗外大喊：“嘿，鲍勃！我能把猫放出去吗？”问题是鲍勃可能听不到她。他可能正在看电视、去女朋友家，或者出去买狗粮了。他们可以试着用手机联系，但如果鲍勃在洗澡、开车经过隧道、或者在给手机充电，同样的困难依然存在。

text:
Alice has a clever idea. She sets up one or more empty beer cans on Bob’s win-
dowsill (Fig. 1.4), ties a string around each one, and runs the string back to her house.
Bob does the same. When she wants to send a signal to Bob, she yanks the string to
knock over one of the cans. When Bob notices a can has been knocked over, he resets
the can.
translated: 爱丽丝想出了一个聪明的主意。她在鲍勃的窗台上放置一个或多个空啤酒罐（图 1.4），在每个罐子上系一根绳子，并将绳子拉回自己的房子。鲍勃也做同样的事情。当她想给鲍勃发送信号时，她拉动绳子打翻其中一个罐子。当鲍勃发现有罐子被打翻时，他将罐子复位。

but what if he goes to Cancún for spring break? As long as Alice relies on Bob to

text:
To prove that the pets will never be in the yard together, assume by way of contra-
diction that there is a way the pets could end up in the yard together. Consider the last
time Alice and Bob each raised their flag and looked at the other’s flag before sending
the pet into the yard. When Alice last looked, her flag was already fully raised. She
must have not seen Bob’s flag, or she would not have released the cat, so Bob must
have not completed raising his flag before Alice started looking. It follows that when
Bob looked for the last time, after raising his flag for the last time, it must have been
after Alice started looking, so he must have seen Alice’s flag raised and would not
have released his dog, a contradiction.
translated: 为了证明宠物永远不会同时在院子里，假设相反情况成立，即存在一种情况让宠物同时出现在院子里。考虑爱丽丝和鲍勃各自最后一次升起旗帜并查看对方旗帜、然后才把宠物放进院子里的时刻。当爱丽丝最后一次查看时，她的旗帜已经完全升起。她一定没看到鲍勃的旗帜，否则就不会放出猫，所以鲍勃一定在爱丽丝开始查看之前没能完成升旗。由此可见，当鲍勃最后一次查看时（在最后一次升旗之后），一定是在爱丽丝开始查看之后，所以他一定看到了爱丽丝的旗帜已升起，便不会放出狗，这就产生了矛盾。

text:
This kind of argument by contradiction shows up over and over again, and it is
worth spending some time understanding why this claim is true. It is important to
note that we never assumed that “raising my flag” or “looking at your flag” happens
instantaneously, nor did we make any assumptions about how long such activities
take. All we care about is when these activities start or end.
translated: 这种反证法论证反复出现，值得花些时间理解为何该命题成立。重要的是要注意，我们从未假设“举起我的旗帜”或“看你的旗帜”是瞬间发生的，也没有对这些活动持续多久做任何假设。我们只关心这些活动何时开始或结束。

text: 1.2.1 Properties of a mutual exclusion protocol
translated: 1.2.1 互斥协议的属性

text:
To show that the flag protocol is a correct solution to Alice and Bob’s problem, we
must understand what properties a solution requires, and then show that the protocol
meets them.
translated: 要证明标志协议是 Alice 和 Bob 问题的正确解决方案，我们必须了解解决方案需要哪些属性，然后证明该协议满足这些属性。

commands.text: 要证明标志协议是 Alice 和 Bob 问题的正确解决方案，我们必须了解解决方案需要哪些属
性，然后证明该协议满足这些属性。

lines: 要证明标志协议是 Alice 和 Bob 问题的正确解决方案，我们必须了解解决方案需要哪些属
性，然后证明该协议满足这些属性。

text:
We already proved that the pets are excluded from being in the yard at the same
time, a property we call mutual exclusion.
translated: 我们已经证明宠物被排除在同时在院子里，这一性质我们称为互斥。

commands.text: 我们已经证明宠物被排除在同时在院子里，这一性质我们称为互斥。

lines: 我们已经证明宠物被排除在同时在院子里，这一性质我们称为互斥。

text:
Mutual exclusion is only one of several properties of interest. After all, a protocol
in which Alice and Bob never release a pet satisfies the mutual exclusion property,
but it is unlikely to satisfy their pets.
translated: 互斥只是几个感兴趣的属性之一。毕竟，一个 Alice 和 Bob 永远不释放宠物的协议满足互斥属性，但不太可能让他们的宠物满意。

commands.text: 互斥只是几个感兴趣的属性之一。毕竟，一个 Alice 和 Bob 永远不释放宠物的协议
满足互斥属性，但不太可能让他们的宠物满意。

lines: 互斥只是几个感兴趣的属性之一。毕竟，一个 Alice 和 Bob 永远不释放宠物的协议
满足互斥属性，但不太可能让他们的宠物满意。

text:
Here is another property of central importance: If only one pet wants to enter
the yard, then it eventually succeeds. In addition, if both pets want to enter the yard,
then eventually at least one of them succeeds. We consider this deadlock-freedom
property to be essential. Note that whereas mutual exclusion is a safety property,
deadlock-freedom is a liveness property.
translated: 这是另一个至关重要的性质：如果只有一只宠物想进入院子，那么它最终会成功。此外，如果两只宠物都想进入院子，那么最终至少有一只会成功。我们认为这种无死锁性质是必不可少的。请注意，互斥是一种安全性质，而无死锁是一种活性质量。

text:
We claim that Alice and Bob’s protocol is deadlock-free. Suppose both pets want
to use the yard. Alice and Bob both raise their flags. Bob eventually notices that
Alice’s flag is raised, and defers to her by lowering his flag, allowing Alice’s cat into
the yard.
translated: 我们声称 Alice 和 Bob 的协议是无死锁的。假设两只宠物都想使用院子。Alice 和 Bob 都升起了他们的旗帜。Bob 最终注意到 Alice 的旗帜升起了，便降下自己的旗帜以示谦让，让 Alice 的猫进入院子。

的旗帜。Bob 最终注意到 Alice 的旗帜升起了，便降下自己的旗帜以示谦让，让 Alice 的猫进入院子

text:
Another property of interest is starvation-freedom (sometimes called lockout-
freedom): If a pet wants to enter the yard, will it eventually succeed? Here, Alice and
Bob’s protocol performs poorly. Whenever Alice and Bob are in conflict, Bob defers
to Alice, so it is possible that Alice’s cat can use the yard over and over again, while
Bob’s dog becomes increasingly uncomfortable. Later on, we consider protocols that
prevent starvation.
translated: 另一个感兴趣的属性是无饥饿性（有时称为无锁定性）：如果一只宠物想进入院子，它最终能成功吗？在这里，爱丽丝和鲍勃的协议表现不佳。每当爱丽丝和鲍勃发生冲突时，鲍勃都会让步给爱丽丝，因此爱丽丝的猫可能反复使用院子，而鲍勃的狗则会变得越来越不舒服。稍后我们将讨论防止饥饿的协议。

text:
The last property of interest concerns waiting. Imagine that Alice raises her flag,
and is then suddenly stricken with appendicitis. She (and the cat) are taken to the
hospital, and after a successful operation, she spends the next week under observation
at the hospital. Although Bob is relieved that Alice is well, his dog cannot use the yard
for an entire week until Alice returns. The problem is that the protocol states that Bob
(and his dog) must wait for Alice to lower her flag. If Alice is delayed (even for a
good reason), then Bob is also delayed (for no apparently good reason).
translated: 最后一个值得关注的属性是关于等待的。假设爱丽丝举起了旗子，随后突然患上了阑尾炎。她（和猫）被送往医院，手术成功后，她在医院观察了整整一周。虽然鲍勃为爱丽丝康复感到欣慰，但他的狗却在爱丽丝回来之前整整一周都无法使用院子。问题在于协议规定鲍勃（和他的狗）必须等待爱丽丝降下旗子。如果爱丽丝延迟了（即使是正当理由），鲍勃也会被延迟（没有明显的正当理由）。

text:
The question of waiting is important as an example of fault-tolerance. Normally,
we expect Alice and Bob to respond to each other in a reasonable amount of time,
but what if they do not do so? The mutual exclusion problem, by its very essence,
requires waiting: No mutual exclusion protocol, no matter how clever, can avoid it.
Nevertheless, we will see that many other coordination problems can be solved with-
out waiting, sometimes in unexpected ways.

text: 1.2.2 The moral

Having reviewed the strengths and weaknesses of Alice and Bob’s protocol, we now
turn our attention back to computer science.
translated: 在回顾了爱丽丝和鲍勃协议的优缺点之后，我们现在将注意力转回计算机科学。

First, we examine why shouting across the yard and placing cell phone calls does
not work. Two kinds of communication occur naturally in concurrent systems:

Mutual exclusion requires persistent communication. The problem with shouting
across the yard or placing cell phone calls is that it may or may not be okay for Bob
to release his dog, but if Alice does not respond to messages, he will never know.

text:
The can-and-string protocol might seem somewhat contrived, but it corresponds
accurately to a common communication protocol in concurrent systems: interrupts.
In modern operating systems, one common way for one thread to get the attention
of another is to send it an interrupt. More precisely, thread A interrupts thread B by
setting a bit at a location periodically checked by B. Sooner or later, B notices the
bit has been set and reacts. After reacting, B typically resets the bit (A cannot reset
the bit). Even though interrupts cannot solve the mutual exclusion problem, they can
still be very useful. For example, interrupt communication is the basis of the Java
language’s wait() and notifyAll() calls.
translated: 罐子绳电话协议看似有点牵强，但它准确对应了并发系统中常见的通信协议：中断。在现代操作系统中，一个线程获取另一个线程注意力的常见方式是发送中断。更准确地说，线程A通过在B定期检查的位置设置一个位来中断线程B。迟早，B会注意到该位已被设置并做出反应。反应后，B通常会重置该位（A无法重置该位）。尽管中断无法解决互斥问题，但它们仍然非常有用。例如，中断通信是Java语言wait()和notifyAll()调用的基础。

On a more positive note, the fable shows that mutual exclusion between two
threads can be solved (however imperfectly) using only two one-bit variables, each
of which can be written by one thread and read by the other.

text: 1.3 The producer–consumer problem
translated: 1.3 生产者-消费者问题

text:
Mutual exclusion is not the only problem worth investigating. Eventually, Alice and
Bob fall in love and marry. Eventually, they divorce. (What were they thinking?) The
judge gives Alice custody of the pets, and tells Bob to feed them. The pets now get
along with one another, but they side with Alice, and attack Bob whenever they see
him. As a result, Alice and Bob need to devise a protocol for Bob to deliver food to
the pets without Bob and the pets being in the yard together. Moreover, the protocol
should not waste anyone’s time: Alice does not want to release her pets into the yard
unless there is food there, and Bob does not want to enter the yard unless the pets have
consumed all the food. This problem is known as the producer–consumer problem.
translated: 互斥不是唯一值得研究的问题。最终，爱丽丝和鲍勃相爱并结婚。最终，他们离婚了（他们当时在想什么？）。法官判给爱丽丝宠物的监护权，并命令鲍勃喂养它们。宠物现在相处融洽，但它们站在爱丽丝一边，一看到鲍勃就攻击他。因此，爱丽丝和鲍勃需要设计一个协议，让鲍勃在不与宠物同时待在院子里的情况下送食物。此外，该协议不应浪费任何人的时间：除非院子里有食物，否则爱丽丝不想把宠物放进院子；除非宠物吃光了所有食物，否则鲍勃不想进入院子。这个问题被称为生产者-消费者问题。

text:
Both this producer–consumer protocol and the earlier mutual exclusion protocol
ensure that Alice and Bob are never in the yard at the same time. However, Alice
and Bob cannot use this producer–consumer protocol for mutual exclusion, and it
is important to understand why: The mutual exclusion problem requires deadlock-
freedom: Each person must be able to enter the yard if it is empty (and the other is not
trying to enter). By contrast, the producer–consumer protocol’s starvation-freedom
property assumes continuous cooperation from both parties.
translated: 这个生产者-消费者协议和前面的互斥协议都确保了 Alice 和 Bob 永远不会同时在院子里。但是，Alice 和 Bob 不能将这个生产者-消费者协议用于互斥，理解原因很重要：互斥问题要求无死锁：如果院子是空的（且另一个人没有试图进入），每个人都必须能够进入院子。相比之下，生产者-消费者协议的无饥饿性质假设双方持续合作。

text:
Mutual exclusion: Instead of a proof by contradiction, as we used earlier, we use
an inductive “state machine”-based proof. Think of the stringed can as a machine
that repeatedly transitions between two states, up and down. To show that mutual
exclusion always holds, we must check that it holds initially, and continues to hold
when transitioning from one state to the other.
translated: 互斥：我们使用基于归纳的"状态机"证明，而不是像之前那样使用反证法。将串罐视为一个在向上和向下两种状态之间反复转换的机器。要证明互斥始终成立，我们必须检查它在初始时成立，并且在从一种状态转换到另一种状态时继续成立。

text:
If this problem is so easy to solve, then why do we bring it up? Both the mutual
exclusion and producer–consumer protocols require waiting: If one participant is sub-
jected to an unexpected delay, then so is the other. In the context of shared-memory
multiprocessors, a solution to the readers–writers problem is a way of allowing a
thread to capture an instantaneous view of several memory locations. Capturing such
a view without waiting, that is, without preventing other threads from modifying these
locations while they are being read, is a powerful tool that can be used for backups,
debugging, and in many other situations. Surprisingly, the readers–writers problem
does have solutions that do not require waiting. We examine several such solutions
in later chapters.
translated: 如果这个问题这么容易解决，那我们为什么还要提出来？互斥协议和生产者-消费者协议都需要等待：如果一个参与者遭遇意外延迟，另一个也会如此。在共享内存多处理器的背景下，读者-写者问题的解决方案是一种让线程捕捉多个内存位置瞬时视图的方法。在不等待的情况下捕捉这种视图，即在读取时不阻止其他线程修改这些位置，是一个强大的工具，可用于备份、调试和许多其他情况。令人惊讶的是，读者-写者问题确实存在不需要等待的解决方案。我们将在后续章节中探讨几种此类解决方案。

text: 1.5 The harsh realities of parallelization
translated: 1.5 并行化的残酷现实

text:
Here is why multiprocessor programming is so much fun. In an ideal world, upgrad-
ing from a uniprocessor to an n-way multiprocessor should provide about an n-fold
increase in computational power. In practice, sadly, this (almost) never happens. The
primary reason is that most real-world computational problems cannot be effectively
parallelized without incurring the costs of interprocessor communication and coordi-
nation.
translated: 这就是多处理器编程如此有趣的原因。在理想世界中，从单处理器升级到 n 路多处理器应该能提供约 n 倍的计算能力提升。遗憾的是，在实践中，这种情况（几乎）从未发生。主要原因是大多数现实世界的计算问题无法在不产生处理器间通信和协调成本的情况下被有效并行化。

text:
Consider five friends who decide to paint a five-room house. If all the rooms are
the same size, then it makes sense to assign each friend to paint one room. As long
as everyone paints at about the same rate, we would get a five-fold speedup over the
single-painter case. The task becomes more complicated if the rooms are of different
sizes. For example, if one room is twice the size of the others, then the five painters
will not achieve a five-fold speedup because the overall completion time is dominated
by the one room that takes the longest to paint.
translated: 考虑五个朋友决定粉刷一栋五居室的房子。如果所有房间大小相同，那么让每个朋友负责粉刷一个房间是合理的。只要每个人的粉刷速度大致相同，我们就能比单人粉刷快五倍。如果房间大小不同，任务就会变得更复杂。例如，如果有一个房间是其他房间的两倍大，那么这五个粉刷工将无法实现五倍的加速，因为整体完成时间取决于粉刷时间最长的那个房间。

text:

we need is called Amdahl’s law. It captures the notion that the extent to which we can
speed up any complex job (not just painting) is limited by how much of the job must
be executed sequentially.

text:
Here is what Amdahl’s law tells us about the utilization of multiprocessor ma-
chines. Some computational problems are “embarrassingly parallel”: they can easily
be divided into components that can be executed concurrently. Such problems some-
times arise in scientific computing or in graphics, but rarely in systems. In general,
however, for a given problem and a 10-processor machine, Amdahl’s law says that
even if we manage to parallelize 90% of the solution, but not the remaining 10%,
then we end up with a five-fold speedup, not a 10-fold speedup. In other words, the
remaining 10% that we did not parallelize cut our utilization of the machine in half.
It seems worthwhile to invest effort to derive as much parallelism from the remaining
10% as possible, even if it is difficult. Typically, it is hard because these additional
parallel parts involve substantial communication and coordination. A major focus of
this book is understanding the tools and techniques that allow programmers to effec-
tively program the parts of the code that require coordination and synchronization,
because the gains made on these parts may have a profound impact on performance.
translated: 阿姆达尔定律告诉我们关于多处理器机器利用率的情况。有些计算问题具有“令人尴尬的并行性”：它们可以轻松分解为可并发执行的组件。这类问题有时出现在科学计算或图形处理中，但在系统领域却很少见。然而一般来说，对于给定的问题和一台10处理器的机器，阿姆达尔定律指出，即使我们设法将90%的解决方案并行化，但剩余的10%未并行化，最终获得的也只是5倍加速，而非10倍加速。换句话说，我们未并行化的那10%将机器利用率减半了。投入精力从剩余的10%中挖掘尽可能多的并行性似乎是值得的，即使这很困难。通常之所以难，是因为这些额外的并行部分涉及大量的通信和协调。本书的一个重点是理解工具和技术，使程序员能够有效地编写需要协调和同步的代码部分，因为在这些部分取得的收益可能对性能产生深远影响。

text:
It would have been simpler to have threads perform these three lines atomically, that
is, in a single mutually exclusive block. Instead, only the call to getAndIncrement() is
atomic. This approach makes sense when we consider the implications of Amdahl’s
law: It is important to minimize the granularity of sequential code, in this case, the
code accessed using mutual exclusion. Moreover, it is important to implement mutual
exclusion in an effective way, since the communication and coordination around the
mutually exclusive shared counter can substantially affect the performance of our
program as a whole.
translated: 如果让线程在单个互斥块中原子性地执行这三行代码，本会更简单。然而，只有对 `getAndIncrement()` 的调用是原子的。考虑到阿姆达尔定律的含义，这种方法是合理的：重要的是将顺序代码的粒度降到最小，这里指的是通过互斥访问的代码。此外，以有效方式实现互斥也很重要，因为围绕互斥共享计数器的通信和协调会显著影响整个程序的性能。

text: 1.6 Parallel programming
translated: 1.6 并行编程

text:
For many of the applications we wish to parallelize, significant parts can easily be
determined as executable in parallel because they do not require any form of coordi-
nation or communication. However, at the time this book is being written, there is no
cookbook recipe for identifying these parts. This is where the application designer
must use his or her accumulated understanding of the algorithm being parallelized.
Luckily, in many cases it is obvious how to identify such parts. The more substantial
problem, the one which this book addresses, is how to deal with the remaining parts
of the program. As noted earlier, these are the parts that cannot be parallelized easily
because the program must access shared data and requires interprocess coordination
and communication in an essential way.
translated: 对于我们希望并行化的许多应用程序，其重要部分很容易被确定为可并行执行，因为它们不需要任何形式的协调或通信。然而，在本书编写之时，尚无识别这些部分的现成秘诀。这正是应用程序设计师必须利用其对被并行化算法的累积理解之处。幸运的是，在许多情况下，如何识别此类部分显而易见。更实质性的问题——即本书所要解决的问题——是如何处理程序的其余部分。如前所述，这些部分难以轻易并行化，因为程序必须以一种根本的方式访问共享数据，并需要进程间的协调和通信。

text:
The goal of this text is to expose the reader to core ideas behind modern coordina-
tion paradigms and concurrent data structures. We present the reader with a unified,
comprehensive picture of the elements that are key to effective multiprocessor pro-
gramming, ranging from basic principles to best-practice engineering techniques.
translated: 本文的目标是让读者接触现代协调范式和并发数据结构背后的核心思想。我们为读者呈现了一个统一、全面的图景，涵盖了高效多处理器编程的关键要素，范围从基本原理到最佳实践工程技术。

一、全面的图景，涵盖了高效多处理器编程的关键要素，范围从基本原理到最佳实践工程技术。

text:
Multiprocessor programming poses many challenges, ranging from grand intel-
lectual issues to subtle engineering tricks. We tackle these challenges using succes-
sive refinement, starting with an idealized model in which mathematical concerns are
paramount, and gradually moving on to more pragmatic models, where we increas-
ingly focus on basic engineering principles.
translated: 多处理器编程带来了许多挑战，范围从重大的智力问题到微妙的工程技巧。我们通过逐步细化来解决这些挑战，从一个数学关切至上的理想化模型开始，逐渐转向更务实的模型，在这些模型中我们越来越关注基本的工程原则。

text:
For example, the first problem we consider is mutual exclusion, the oldest and still
one of the fundamental problems in the field. We begin with a mathematical perspec-
tive, analyzing the computability and correctness properties of various algorithms on
an idealized architecture. The algorithms themselves, while classical, are not practi-
cal for modern multicore architectures. Nevertheless, learning how to reason about
such idealized algorithms is an important step toward learning how to reason about
more realistic (and more complex) algorithms. It is particularly important to learn
how to reason about subtle liveness issues such as starvation and deadlock.
translated: 例如，我们考虑的第一个问题是互斥，这是该领域最古老且仍然是最基础的问题之一。我们从数学角度出发，在理想化架构上分析各种算法的可计算性和正确性。这些算法虽然经典，但不适用于现代多核架构。然而，学习如何推理此类理想化算法，是学习如何推理更现实（也更复杂）算法的重要一步。特别重要的是要学习如何推理微妙的活性问题，如饥饿和死锁。

text:
Once we understand how to reason about such algorithms in general, we turn
our attention to more realistic contexts. We explore a variety of algorithms and data
structures using different multiprocessor architectures with the goal of understanding
which are effective, and why.
translated: 一旦我们理解了如何一般性地推理此类算法，我们便将注意力转向更现实的场景。我们使用不同的多处理器架构探索各种算法和数据结构，旨在了解哪些是有效的，以及为什么有效。

text:
Most of the parable of Alice and Bob is adapted from Leslie Lamport’s invited lec-
ture at the 1984 ACM Symposium on Principles of Distributed Computing [104].
The readers–writers problem is a classical synchronization problem that has received
attention in numerous papers over the past 20 years. Amdahl’s law is due to Gene
Amdahl, a parallel processing pioneer [9].

text:
Exercise 1.1. The dining philosophers problem was invented by E.W. Dijkstra, a con-
currency pioneer, to clarify the notions of deadlock- and starvation-freedom. Imagine
five philosophers who spend their lives just thinking and feasting on rice. They sit
around a circular table, illustrated in Fig. 1.5. However, there are only five chopsticks

text:
1. Write a program to simulate the behavior of the philosophers, where each philoso-
pher is a thread and the chopsticks are shared objects. Note that you must prevent
a situation where two philosophers hold the same chopstick at the same time.
translated: 1. 编写一个程序来模拟哲学家的行为，其中每个哲学家是一个线程，筷子是共享对象。注意，你必须防止两个哲学家同时持有同一根筷子的情况。

意，你必须防止两个哲学家同时持有同一根筷子的情况。

text:
2. Amend your program so that it never reaches a state where philosophers are dead-
locked, that is, it is never the case that every philosopher holds one chopstick and
is stuck waiting for another to get the second chopstick.
translated: 2. 修改你的程序，使其永远不会达到哲学家们死锁的状态，也就是说，永远不会出现每个哲学家都拿着一根筷子并卡在等待另一根筷子以获取第二根筷子的情况。

text: 3. Amend your program so that no philosopher ever starves.
translated: 3. 修改你的程序，使得没有哲学家会挨饿。

text:
4. Write a program to provide a starvation-free solution for n philosophers for any
natural number n.
translated: 4. 编写一个程序，为任意自然数 n 的 n 位哲学家提供无饥饿解决方案。

text:
Exercise 1.2. For each of the following, state whether it is a safety or liveness prop-
erty. Identify the bad or good thing of interest.
translated: 练习 1.2. 对于下列各项，判断其是安全性质还是活性质量。识别相关的坏事或好事。

commands.text: 练习 1.2. 对于下列各项，判断其是安全性质还是活性质量。识别相关的坏事或好事

lines: 练习 1.2. 对于下列各项，判断其是安全性质还是活性质量。识别相关的坏事或好事

text: 1. Patrons are served in the order they arrive.
translated: 1. 顾客按到达顺序接受服务。

text: 2. Anything that can go wrong, will go wrong.
translated: 凡是可能出错的事，终将出错。

text: 3. No one wants to die.
translated: 3.  没有人想死。

text: 4. Two things are certain: death and taxes.
translated: 4. 世界上只有两件事是确定的：死亡和税收。

text: 5. As soon as one is born, one starts dying.
translated: 5. 一生下来，就开始走向死亡。

text: 6. If an interrupt occurs, then a message is printed within one second.
translated: 6. 如果发生中断，则会在一秒内打印一条消息。

text: 7. If an interrupt occurs, then a message is printed.
translated: 7. 如果发生中断，则会打印一条消息。

text: 8. I will finish what Darth Vader has started.
translated: 8. 我将完成达斯·维德未竟的事业。

text: 9. The cost of living never decreases.
translated: 9. 生活成本从不降低。

text: 10. You can always tell a Harvard man.
translated: 你总能认出哈佛毕业生。

text:
Exercise 1.3. In the producer–consumer fable, we assumed that Bob can see whether
the can on Alice’s windowsill is up or down. Design a producer–consumer protocol
using cans and strings that works even if Bob cannot see the state of Alice’s can (this
is how real-world interrupt bits work).
translated: 练习 1.3. 在生产者–消费者寓言中，我们假设 Bob 可以看到 Alice 窗台上的罐子是竖起还是放下。设计一个使用罐子和绳子的生产者–消费者协议，使其即使在 Bob 无法看到 Alice 罐子状态时也能工作（这就是现实世界中断位的工作方式）。

text:
Exercise 1.4. You are one of P recently arrested prisoners. The warden, a deranged
computer scientist, makes the following announcement:
translated: 练习 1.4。你是最近被捕的 P 名囚犯之一。典狱长是一位疯狂的计算机科学家，宣布道：

commands.text: 练习 1.4。你是最近被捕的 P 名囚犯之一。典狱长是一位疯狂的计算机科学家，宣
布道：

lines: 练习 1.4。你是最近被捕的 P 名囚犯之一。典狱长是一位疯狂的计算机科学家，宣
布道：

text:
You may meet together today and plan a strategy, but after today you will be in
isolated cells and have no communication with one another.
translated: 你们可以今天聚在一起制定策略，但从今天之后你们将被关进单独的牢房，无法相互沟通。

text:
I have set up a “switch room” which contains a light switch, which is either on or
off. The switch is not connected to anything.
translated: 我设了一个“开关房间”，里面装着一个电灯开关，要么开着要么关着。这开关什么也没连。

text:
Every now and then, I will select one prisoner at random to enter the “switch
room.” This prisoner may throw the switch (from on to off, or vice versa), or may
leave the switch unchanged. Nobody else will ever enter this room.
translated: 不时地，我会随机选择一名囚犯进入“开关室”。这名囚犯可以拨动开关（从开到关，或从关到开），也可以不改变开关状态。其他人绝不会进入这个房间。

once.” Ifthe claim is correct, I will set youfree. Ifthe claim is incorrect, I willfeed

text:
Exercise 1.5. The same warden has a different idea. He orders the prisoners to stand
in line, and places red and blue hats on each of their heads. No prisoner knows the
color of his own hat, or the color of any hat behind him, but he can see the hats of
the prisoners in front. The warden starts at the back of the line and asks each prisoner
to guess the color of his own hat. The prisoner can answer only “red” or “blue.” If
he gives the wrong answer, he is fed to the crocodiles. If he answers correctly, he is
freed. Each prisoner can hear the answer of the prisoners behind him, but cannot tell
whether that prisoner was correct.
translated: 练习 1.5. 同一典狱长有了不同的主意。他命令囚犯排成一行，并在每人头上戴上红帽或蓝帽。没有囚犯知道自己帽子的颜色，也不知道身后任何帽子的颜色，但他能看到前面囚犯的帽子。典狱长从队尾开始，询问每个囚犯猜自己帽子的颜色。囚犯只能回答"红色"或"蓝色"。如果回答错误，他会被喂给鳄鱼。如果回答正确，他会被释放。每个囚犯都能听到身后囚犯的回答，但无法判断那名囚犯是否回答正确。

text:
Exercise 1.6. A financial risk management program is sped up by making 85% of
the application concurrent, while 15% remains sequential. However, it turns out that
during a concurrent execution the number of cache misses grows in a way dependent
on N, the number of cores used. The dependency is\begin{array} { r } { C a c h e M i s s = \frac { N ^ { \bullet } } { N + 1 0 } } \end{array}. Profiling
translated: 练习 1.6. 一个金融风险管理程序通过将 85% 的应用程序并行化而加速，而 15% 仍然是串行的。然而，发现在并发执行期间，缓存未命中的数量以一种依赖于 N（使用的核心数）的方式增长。这种依赖关系是\begin{array} { r } { C a c h e M i s s = \frac { N ^ { \bullet } } { N + 1 0 } } \end{array}。性能分析

text:
the program reveals that 20% of the operations performed are memory accesses for
both the sequential and parallel parts. The cost of other operations, including cache
accesses, is 1 unit, and accessing memory has a cost of 3N 11 units for the par-
allel part and a cost of 14 for the sequential part. Compute the optimal number of
processors on which the program should run.
translated: 程序显示，执行的操作中有20%是内存访问，这对顺序部分和并行部分都适用。其他操作（包括缓存访问）的成本为1个单位，而访问内存对于并行部分的成本为3N+11个单位，对于顺序部分的成本为14个单位。计算程序应运行的最优处理器数量。

text:

text: Mutual exclusion
translated: 互斥

text:
Mutual exclusion is perhaps the most prevalent form of coordination in multipro-
cessor programming. This chapter covers classical mutual exclusion algorithms that
work by reading and writing shared memory. Although these algorithms are not used
in practice, we study them because they provide an ideal introduction to the kinds
of algorithmic and correctness issues that arise in every area of synchronization. The
chapter also provides an impossibility proof. This proof teaches us the limitations
of solutions to mutual exclusion that work by reading and writing shared memory,
which helps to motivate the real-world mutual exclusion algorithms that appear in
later chapters. This chapter is one of the few that contains proofs of algorithms.
Though the reader should feel free to skip these proofs, it is helpful to understand
the kind of reasoning they present, because we can use the same approach to reason
about the practical algorithms considered in later chapters.
translated: 互斥可能是多处理器编程中最常见的协调形式。本章介绍通过读写共享内存工作的经典互斥算法。尽管这些算法在实践中不使用，我们仍然研究它们，因为它们为同步领域中出现的各种算法和正确性问题提供了理想的入门介绍。本章还提供了一个不可行性证明。这个证明让我们了解通过读写共享内存解决互斥的局限性，这有助于激发后续章节中出现的真实世界互斥算法。本章是极少数包含算法证明的章节之一。虽然读者可以自由跳过这些证明，但了解它们所呈现的推理类型是有帮助的，因为我们可以用同样的方法来推理后续章节中考虑的实用算法。

text: 2.1 Time and events
translated: 2.1 时间与事件

text:
Reasoning about concurrent computation is mostly reasoning about time. Sometimes
we want things to happen simultaneously, and sometimes we want them to happen at
different times. To reason about complicated conditions involving how multiple time
intervals can overlap, or how they cannot, we need a simple but unambiguous lan-
guage to talk about events and durations in time. Everyday English is too ambiguous
and imprecise. Instead, we introduce a simple vocabulary and notation to describe
how concurrent threads behave in time.
translated: 对并发计算的推理主要是对时间的推理。有时我们希望事件同时发生，有时则希望它们在不同时间发生。要推理涉及多个时间区间如何重叠或不重叠的复杂条件，我们需要一种简单且无歧义的语言来描述时间中的事件和持续时间。日常英语过于模糊和不精确。因此，我们引入了一套简单的词汇和符号来描述并发线程在时间中的行为。

In 1687, Isaac Newton wrote, “Absolute, True, and Mathematical Time, of itself,
and from its own nature flows equably without relation to any thing external.” We en-
dorse his notion of time, if not his prose style. Threads share a common time (though
not necessarily a common clock). A thread is a state machine, and its state transitions
are called events.

text: 2.2 Critical sections
translated: 2.2 临界区

text:
In Chapter 1, we discussed the Counter class implementation shown in Fig. 2.1. We
observed that this implementation is correct in a single-thread system, but misbehaves
when used by two or more threads. The problem occurs if both threads read the value
field at the line marked “start of danger zone,” and then both update that field at the
line marked “end of danger zone.”
translated: 在第 1 章中，我们讨论了图 2.1 所示的 Counter 类实现。我们观察到该实现在单线程系统中是正确的，但在被两个或更多线程使用时会出现错误行为。如果两个线程都在标记为“危险区开始”的行读取 value 字段，然后都在标记为“危险区结束”的行更新该字段，就会出现问题。

，但在被两个或更多线程使用时会出现错误行为。如果两个线程都在标记为“危险区开始”的行读取
value 字段，然后都在标记为“危险区结束”的行更新该字段，就会出现问题。

，但在被两个或更多线程使用时会出现错误行为。如果两个线程都在标记为“危险区开始”的行读取
value 字段，然后都在标记为“危险区结束”的行更新该字段，就会出现问题。

We can avoid this problem by making these two lines into a critical section: a
block of code that can be executed by only one thread at a time. We call this property
mutual exclusion. The standard way to achieve mutual exclusion is through a Lock
object satisfying the interface shown in Fig. 2.2.

text: 1. each critical section is associated with a Lock object,
translated: 1. 每个临界区都与一个 Lock 对象相关联，

text:
2. the thread calls that object’s lock() method when it wants to enter the critical
section, and
translated: 2. 当线程想要进入临界区时，它会调用该对象的 lock() 方法，并且

text: 3. the thread calls the unlock() method when it leaves the critical section.
translated: 3. 线程在离开临界区时调用 unlock() 方法。

text:
We say that a thread acquires (alternatively, locks) a lock when it returns from a
lock() method call, and releases (alternatively, unlocks) the lock when it invokes the
unlock() method. If a thread has acquired and not subsequently released a lock, we
say that the thread holds the lock. No thread may acquire the lock while any other
thread holds it, so at most one thread holds the lock at any time. We say the lock is
busy if a thread holds it; otherwise, we say the lock is free.
translated: 当线程从 `lock()` 方法调用返回时，我们说该线程**获取**（或**锁定**）了锁；当它调用 `unlock()` 方法时，我们说该线程**释放**（或**解锁**）了锁。如果一个线程已获取锁且随后未释放，我们说该线程**持有**该锁。只要有其他线程持有锁，任何线程都无法获取该锁，因此在任意时刻最多只有一个线程持有锁。如果有线程持有锁，我们说该锁是**忙碌**的；否则，我们说该锁是**空闲**的。

空闲**的。

Multiple critical sections may be associated with the same Lock, in which case
no thread may execute a critical section while any other thread is executing a critical
section associated with the same Lock. From the perspective of a Lock algorithm, a
thread starts a critical section when its call to the lock() method returns, and it ends
the critical section by invoking the unlock() method; that is, a thread executes the
critical section while it holds the lock.
translated: 多个临界区可以与同一个 Lock 关联，在这种情况下，当任何其他线程正在执行与同一个 Lock 关联的临界区时，任何线程都不能执行临界区。从 Lock 算法的角度来看，当线程对 lock() 方法的调用返回时，它开始临界区，并通过调用 unlock() 方法结束临界区；也就是说，线程在持有锁时执行临界区。

We now state more precisely the properties that a good Lock algorithm should
satisfy, assuming that every thread that acquires the lock eventually releases it.

text: Mutual exclusion At most one thread holds the lock at any time.
translated: 互斥 在任意时刻最多只有一个线程持有锁。

text:
Freedom from deadlock If a thread is attempting to acquire or release the lock
(i.e., it invoked lock() or unlock() and has not returned), then eventually some
thread acquires or releases the lock (i.e., it returns from invoking lock() or
unlock()). If a thread calls lock() and never returns, then other threads must
complete an infinite number of critical sections.
translated: 死锁自由性 如果一个线程正在尝试获取或释放锁（即它调用了 lock() 或 unlock() 且尚未返回），那么最终某个线程将获取或释放该锁（即它从调用 lock() 或 unlock() 中返回）。如果某个线程调用 lock() 后永不返回，则其他线程必须完成无限数量的临界区执行。

那么最终某个线程将获取或释放该锁（即它从调用 lock() 或 unlock() 中返回）。如果某个线程调用
lock() 后永不返回，则其他线程必须完成无限数量的临界区执行。

lock() 后永不返回，则其他线程必须完成无限数量的临界区执行。

text:
Freedom from starvation Every thread that attempts to acquire or release the lock
eventually succeeds (i.e., every call to lock() or unlock() eventually returns).

都会返回）。

都会返回）。

text: Note that starvation-freedom implies deadlock-freedom.

text:
The mutual exclusion property is clearly essential. It guarantees that the critical
section, that is, the code executed between the acquisition and release of the lock, is
executed by at most one thread at a time. In other words, executions of the critical sec-
tion cannot overlap. Without this property, we cannot guarantee that a computation’s
results are correct.
translated: 互斥属性显然是必不可少的。它保证临界区（即在获取和释放锁之间执行的代码）在任何时候最多只能由一个线程执行。换句话说，临界区的执行不能重叠。没有这个属性，我们就无法保证计算结果的正确性。

text:
The deadlock-freedom property is important. It implies that the system never
“freezes.” If some thread calls lock() and never acquires the lock, then either some
other thread acquires and never releases the lock or other threads must be completing
an infinite number of critical sections. Individual threads may be stuck forever (called
starvation), but some thread makes progress.
translated: 无死锁特性至关重要。它意味着系统永远不会“冻结”。如果某个线程调用 lock() 却永远无法获取锁，那么要么有其他线程获取了锁且永不释放，要么其他线程必须在执行无限数量的临界区。单个线程可能永远卡住（称为饥饿），但总有某个线程在取得进展。

text:
The starvation-freedom property, while clearly desirable, is the least compelling
of the three. This property is sometimes called lockout-freedom. In later chapters,
we discuss practical mutual exclusion algorithms that are not starvation-free. These
algorithms are typically deployed in circumstances where starvation is a theoretical
possibility, but is unlikely to occur in practice. Nevertheless, the ability to reason
about starvation is essential for understanding whether it is a realistic threat.
translated: 饥饿自由性虽然显然是可取的，但却是这三个性质中最不令人信服的。这一性质有时也被称为闭锁自由。在后面的章节中，我们将讨论一些并非饥饿自由的实用互斥算法。这些算法通常部署在饥饿只是理论上可能、但在实践中不太可能发生的场景中。尽管如此，推理饥饿情况的能力对于理解其是否构成现实威胁至关重要。

each thread. To acquire the lock, a thread sets its flag to true and waits until the other
thread’s flag isfalse. The thread releases the flag by setting its flag back tofalse.

text:
The LockTwo algorithm is inadequate because it gets stuck unless the threads run
concurrently. Nevertheless, LockTwo has an interesting property: If the threads run
concurrently, the lock() method succeeds. The LockOne and LockTwo classes comple-
ment one another: Each succeeds under conditions that cause the other to get stuck.
translated: LockTwo算法是不充分的，因为除非线程并发运行，否则它会卡住。然而，LockTwo 有一个有趣的性质：如果线程并发运行，lock() 方法就会成功。LockOne 和 LockTwo 类相互补充：每个类在导致另一个类卡住的条件下都能成功。

text: 2.3.3 The Peterson lock
translated: 2.3.3 Peterson锁

text:
We combine the LockOne and LockTwo algorithms to construct a starvation-free lock
algorithm, shown in Fig. 2.6. This algorithm—known as Peterson’s algorithm, after
its inventor—is arguably the most succinct and elegant two-thread mutual exclusion
algorithm.
translated: 我们将 LockOne 和 LockTwo 算法结合起来，构建了一个无饥饿锁算法，如图 2.6 所示。该算法被称为 Peterson 算法，以其发明者命名，可以说是最简洁优雅的两线程互斥算法。

text: 2.4 Notes on deadlock
translated: 2.4 关于死锁的说明

text:
Although the Peterson lock algorithm is deadlock-free (and even starvation-free),
another kind of deadlock can arise in programs that use multiple Peterson locks (or
any other lock implementation). For example, suppose that threads A and B share
locks\ell _ { 0 }and\ell _ { 1 }, and that A acquires\ell _ { 0 }and B acquires\ell _ { 1 }. If A then tries to acquire
\ell _ { 1 }and B tries to acquire\ell _ { 0 } ., the threads deadlock because each one waits for the other
to release its lock.
translated: 尽管 Peterson 锁算法无死锁（甚至无饥饿），但在使用多个 Peterson 锁（或任何其他锁实现）的程序中，仍可能出现另一种死锁。例如，假设线程 A 和 B 共享锁 \ell _ { 0 } 和 \ell _ { 1 }，A 获取 \ell _ { 0 } 而 B 获取 \ell _ { 1 }。如果 A 尝试获取 \ell _ { 1 } 而 B 尝试获取 \ell _ { 0 }，线程就会死锁，因为每个线程都在等待另一个线程释放其锁。

text:
In the literature, the term deadlock is sometimes used more narrowly to refer to
the case in which the system enters a state from which there is no way for threads
to make progress. The LockOne and LockTwo algorithms are susceptible to this kind of
deadlock: In both algorithms, both threads can get stuck waiting in their respective
while loops.
translated: 在文献中，术语 deadlock 有时被狭义地用来指代系统进入一种状态，在这种状态下线程无法取得任何进展。LockOne 和 LockTwo 算法都容易受到这种 deadlock 的影响：在这两种算法中，两个线程都可能卡在各自的 while 循环中等待。

lines: 在文献中，术语 deadlock 有时被狭义地用来指代系统进入一种状态，在这种状态下线程无法取得任

text:
This narrower notion of deadlock is distinguished from livelock, in which two
or more threads actively prevent each other from making progress by taking steps
that subvert steps taken by other threads. When the system is livelocked rather than
deadlocked, there is some way to schedule the threads so that the system can make
progress (but also some way to schedule them so that there is no progress). Our
definition of deadlock-freedom proscribes livelock as well as this narrower notion of
deadlock.
translated: 这种更狭义的死锁概念与活锁有所区别，活锁是指两个或更多线程通过采取破坏其他线程所采取步骤的步骤，主动阻止彼此取得进展。当系统处于活锁而非死锁状态时，存在某种线程调度方式使系统能够取得进展（但也存在某种调度方式导致无法取得进展）。我们对无死锁的定义同时排除了活锁和这种更狭义的死锁概念。

text:
However, Livelock does not deadlock by the narrower definition because there is
always some way to schedule the threads so that one of them makes progress: If one
thread’s flag is false, then execute the other thread until it exits the loop and returns.
If both threads’ flag variables are true, then execute one thread until it sets its flag
to false, and then execute the other as described above (i.e., until it returns).
translated: 然而，根据更狭义的定义，活锁并不构成死锁，因为总存在某种线程调度方式，使得其中一个线程能够取得进展：如果某个线程的标志为假，则执行另一个线程直到它退出循环并返回。如果两个线程的标志变量均为真，则先执行其中一个线程直到它将标志设为假，然后按上述方式执行另一个线程（即直到它返回）。

text:
The Peterson lock uses a two-element Boolean flag array to indicate whether a
thread is trying to enter the critical section. The Filter lock generalizes this notion
with an n-element integer level array, where the value of level A indicates the
highest level that thread A is trying to enter. Each thread must pass through n 1
levels of “exclusion” to enter its critical section. Each level - has a distinct victim -
field used to “filter out” one thread, excluding it from that level unless no thread is at
that level or higher.
